violet-wash.purpose: 10-15% alpha of Deep Violet Ink — the tinted background behind the primary Button and chips. Not an independent hue, always derived from the accent.

violet-border.purpose: 40-50% alpha of Deep Violet Ink — hover border color on BentoTiles and the active state on pill toggles.

particle-violet.purpose: Deliberately more saturated than the accent — small low-opacity hero particle dots need stronger contrast than text/UI to stay visible against the cream background.

parchment-cream.purpose: Page background and the surface color for flat cards. Dark mode intentionally breaks the warm hue family and reuses a cool gray/navy neutral rather than a dark-brown version of cream — a deliberate asymmetry, not an oversight.

parchment-shaded.purpose: A step warmer/darker than the page — the code panel and fixed InfoPanel background, so they read as a distinct layer.

section-alt.purpose: Alternating full-section background so consecutive scroll-snap sections read as distinct pages.

parchment-border.purpose: Default 1px border on cards, tiles, dividers, and the code line-number rule.

ink.purpose: Body text color. Dark mode reuses the cool gray/navy neutral family, same asymmetry as Parchment Cream.

ink-deep.purpose: Heading text color — h1/h2/h3, card titles, InfoPanel name block.

display.purpose: Hero h1 only — the largest, boldest moment in the type system.

headline.purpose: The InfoPanel's large section label (e.g. "Experience") — the one other place a heading reaches display scale.

title.purpose: h2 — section and card headings throughout the page.

body.purpose: Default running text, set globally on :root.

label.purpose: Tags, chips, dates, and other small metadata.

mono.purpose: Code samples, inline code, file paths.

shadows.name: floating-surface
shadows.purpose: The system's only shadow. Used exclusively on the Modal and the fixed-position InfoPanel — the two elements genuinely floating above the page.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Default hover/active transition for background, text, and border-color changes — buttons, nav links, badges, pill toggles.

motion.name: ease-panel
motion.purpose: InfoPanel show/hide (opacity + translateY) and its per-section content crossfade.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one call-to-action-style control in the system — violet-tinted at rest, fully inverts to solid violet on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 10px 24px 6px; border-radius: 4px; border: 2px solid var(--accent); background: var(--accent-bg); color: var(--accent); font-family: var(--heading); font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent); color: var(--bg); border-color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Chip / Tag
components.description: Filled, borderless informational tag — case study tags, experience stack items.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; font-size: 12px; color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-bg); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; }

components.name: Pill Toggle
components.description: Outlined, selectable control — framework/language switcher tabs. Active state is a border+text color shift, never a fill, distinguishing it from the filled informational Chip.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 999px; background: none; color: var(--text); font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-pill:hover { border-color: var(--accent-border); } .ds-pill[data-state='checked'] { border-color: var(--accent-border); color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat, bordered container shared by Experience cards, BentoTiles, and FramedImage — 12px radius, no shadow, border-color shift on hover where interactive.
components.html:
QA Lead

Own QA strategy and the release process across the product suite.
components.css: .ds-card { border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 12px; padding: 20px 24px; background: var(--bg); transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: var(--accent-border); } .ds-card-title { font-family: var(--heading); font-weight: 500; font-size: 24px; color: var(--text-h); margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 15px; line-height: 145%; color: var(--text); margin: 0; }

components.name: Modal
components.description: Centered overlay dialog — the system's one shadow token, 12px radius, dark backdrop.
components.html:
Case Study Title

Problem, approach, and outcome go here.
components.css: .ds-modal-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.6); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 20px; } .ds-modal { position: relative; background: var(--bg); border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 10px 24px -8px rgba(60,40,10,0.12); max-width: 560px; width: 100%; padding: 32px 24px 24px; } .ds-modal-close { position: absolute; top: 12px; right: 12px; width: 28px; height: 28px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: none; background: none; color: var(--text); font-size: 20px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-modal-close:hover { color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Display-face navigation link — desktop inline list and the mobile full-screen overlay share this same style.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: var(--heading); color: var(--text); text-decoration: none; font-size: 1rem; transition: color 0.2s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: var(--accent); } .ds-nav-link.active { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: Shiki-rendered code panel on the Parchment Shaded surface — mono type, CSS-counter line numbers with a right-border divider.
components.html: test('logs in', async ({ page }) => {
components.css: .ds-code { margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: var(--code-bg); overflow-x: auto; font-family: ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 13px; line-height: 145%; tab-size: 2; } .ds-code-line { counter-increment: line-number; display: inline; } .ds-line-no::before { content: counter(line-number); display: inline-block; width: 2em; margin-right: 16px; padding-right: 8px; border-right: 1px solid var(--border); text-align: right; color: var(--text); opacity: 0.5; user-select: none; }

narrative.overview:
This is a warm cream page with violet ink on it — the visual language of a working notebook kept by someone who builds things carefully and writes down why. The parchment background and single violet accent read as handmade and personal rather than templated; the custom display face (TBJ Orcherum Mini) gives headings a distinct, slightly graphic voice while body copy stays in a plain, legible system sans, the way a notebook's marginalia is bolder than its running text. Monospace code samples sit on their own slightly-darker "shaded page" surface, like a pasted-in printout.

The system is deliberately restrained: one accent color, two border-radius steps plus a pill for toggles, and almost no shadow — surfaces announce interactivity by a border-color shift, not by lifting off the page. This is a quietly confident, crafted personality, explicitly not the glassy-gradient, stock-photo "AI-generated landing page" look, and explicitly not playful or cartoonish — the personal touches (music, sports, the balsa-wood-bridge story) live inside this same restrained type system rather than spinning up their own decorative treatment.

An alternate Mono theme exists (data-theme="mono") — same structure, a cooler near-white page and a slightly brighter violet — for a visitor who wants a plainer, less warm-toned reading surface. It is a second page in the same notebook, not a different book: every rule applies to both.
keyCharacteristics: Warm parchment-cream page, one deep-violet accent, near-zero decorative color
A custom display face reserved for headings and emphasis; body copy stays in a plain system sans
Flat, bordered surfaces; hover means a border-color shift, not elevation
Shadow appears only on the two things that actually float above the page (Modal, the fixed InfoPanel)
Full-viewport scroll-snap sections, read top to bottom like turning pages

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only color allowed to carry meaning. It appears exclusively on interactive and emphasis moments — never as a decorative fill, background wash on a whole section, or gradient.

rules.name: The Notebook Voice Rule
rules.body: TBJ Orcherum Mini is reserved for headings, nav labels, button labels, and the InfoPanel's name/title block — anywhere text is acting as a label or headline. It never appears in a paragraph of running prose.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, tiles, badges, and buttons never receive a box-shadow. Interactivity is signaled by a border-color shift to violet on hover. Shadow is reserved for things structurally floating above the content.

rules.name: The Three-Radius Rule
rules.body: 4px, 12px, or 999px — nothing in between. A new component reaches for one of these three, never a custom radius value.

dos: Do reserve Deep Violet Ink for interactive and emphasis moments only — links, active states, CTAs, tags. Never a section background or decorative fill.
Do use TBJ Orcherum Mini only for headings, labels, and button text; keep all running prose in the plain system sans.
Do signal card/tile interactivity with a border-color shift to violet on hover — not a shadow, not a lift, not a scale transform.
Do reuse --content-width, --page-gutter, and --content-clearance-desktop for anything that must align to the shared reading column, instead of hardcoding a margin or width.
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion fallback — every existing motion pattern in the system already does this.
donts: Don't add box-shadow to cards, tiles, chips, or buttons. --shadow is reserved for the Modal and the fixed InfoPanel — the only two elements genuinely floating above the page.
Don't introduce a fourth border-radius value. 4px / 12px / 999px is the complete scale, each with one specific job.
Don't reach for a gradient hero, glossy surface, or stock photography — the palette is flat parchment plus one violet accent, full stop.
Don't give the personal/music side of About (WRTHY, DJ sets, rec sports) its own visual treatment or color — it stays inside the existing type system as supporting texture, not a second brand.
